#6687. 7 Celebrity-Approved Ways to Wear Flats With Jeans This Fall

Stylish celebrities confirm that the timeless duo is also one of the coolest.

Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

Today, the humble flat has become just as much of a wardrobe staple as a trusty pair of jeans. And styling them together? That’s practically a no-brainer. Everything from classic ballet flats and loafers to ornate Mary Janes looks especially sharp with structured, dark-wash denim and can instantly elevate baggy or light-wash jeans. With a seemingly infinite selection of chic designs in both categories, it’s an easy-to-repeat formula for all kinds of occasions: strolling through your city on the weekend, exploring a new one, heading into the office, or dressing for a night out.

Some of the most fashionable celebrities are making the combo look cooler than ever, which is why we’ve spotlighted a few of our favorite Hollywood-approved jeans-and-flats getups to inspire your upcoming outfits. From supermodels like Bella Hadid and Kendall Jenner to Zoë Kravitz, find seven impeccable flats-and-jeans ensembles worth copying this fall.

Offset simple black ballet flats and a matching cropped cardigan with a pair of no-waistband jeans, à la Zoë Kravitz. Topped off with a pear-cut tennis necklace, the look is the epitome of elegance with an edge.

Aritzia HomeStretch Rib Spectrum Cami Tank

Schutz Arissa Leather Bow Ballerina Flats

Pointed-toe flats and a sweeping trench make for a flawless French girl-inspired fall outfit. Kendall Jenner wore the duo last year in Paris with crisp, ankle-length mom jeans and a sleek top-handle bag for a chic business-casual vibe.

Rag & Bone Cam Low-Rise Ankle Straight Jeans

Michael Kors Hamilton Large Leather Tote Bag

A sleek leather loafer can work just as well outside the office with relaxed-fit straight-leg jeans and a patterned knit. Striped pullovers are trending this season, as are croc-embossed bags to top off the look. For a touch of elevated Y2K nostalgia, mirror Bella Hadid’s approach and add a grommeted belt in rich leather.

Aritzia Plush Wool Cashmere Poem Turtleneck

Madewell The Straight Jean in Super Stretch Denim

Brahmin Denise Croc Embossed Leather Tote

From bejeweled to feathered and embroidered, embellished shoes had a huge moment on fall 2026 runways. For milder fall days—and to wear again next spring—style a delicate, adorned sheer flat with a timeless, supermodel-worthy trio: a white button-down, bootcut jeans, and a timeless leather belt. Finish with a retro-inspired zigzag headband the It girls are also loving right now.

Designers, street style stars, and A-list celebrities agree: burgundy flats—a more versatile take on bright red styles—belong in your closet this autumn. During a recent press event for Verity, Dakota Johnson wore Khaite’s Jane glove flats with distressed light-wash jeans, a black top, and a cropped plaid Nili Lotan blazer—proving that, with the right styling, a jeans-and-flats combo can be an equally effortless alternative to a polished dress you might otherwise reach for. Reformation’s Blaine flat and A.L.C.’s Cass jacket offer somewhat more accessible ways to recreate Johnson’s look.

Good American Vintage Straight Ankle Jeans

A mention of this season’s top flat trends wouldn’t be complete without ultra-popular jazz-inspired silhouettes. Eva Chen undoubtedly has a penchant for them, having been spotted wearing them with baggy jeans twice this year. Follow suit and style the pairing with a colorful sweater layered over a thin turtleneck for a look that can take you from lounging to a casual lunch.

Textured flats might actually be a bit groundbreaking for fall. Katie Holmes proves the traditionally summer-ready style can add eclectic flair to voluminous jeans and a chunky sweater, especially when teamed with thin crew socks for added warmth. Thrown over her shoulder? A spacious, sumptuous suede tote in a deep ink-blue shade.

#6685. The Real-Life Wardrobe of Jamie Campbell Bower, Who Only Wears Suits If They’re McQueen

“I don’t know, I suppose I’m an artist,” Jamie Campbell Bower says with a laugh, after I ask him to describe himself. He’s correct, in more ways than one. If you’ve been consuming pop culture for the last decade and change, it’s less a matter of if you’ve seen the 37-year-old Londoner before, but where. He’s acted in some of the biggest franchises in Hollywood—including Twilight, Harry Potter, The Mortal Instruments, and Stranger Things—while also nurturing a multifaceted music career. As of this month, he’ll be heading to Middle-earth as Celeborn in the third season of Amazon Prime’s epic Lord of the Rings series, The Rings of Power.

During a hectic week of Rings of Power in New York City, Bower and I spent a quiet early morning talking about the bands that helped him find his style as a teenager, the difference between performing as an actor and a musician, and why he loves playing the bad guy.

All clothing and accessories, subject’s own. Coat by MM6 Maison Margiela. Sweater by John Lawrence Sullivan. Vintage skirt. Shoes by John Lawrence Sullivan. Sunglasses by Persol (throughout). Jewelry by Pianegonda.

Jamie Campbell Bower: It’s complexity. With any character, there has to be a level of complexity. Playing in the shadow self is really illuminating, to be Jungian. You have to know it in order for it to not take over. I found it particularly interesting to rationale and reason, even though this character was doing terrible things. I have always found it really interesting to dig away and find the why. So much of that character was really about isolation and pain and not feeling like they had a sense of belonging in the space for them. Obviously, they find this power that gives them this sense of safety. It becomes the wall, and it gives them purpose, and it hides them from the world and from being hurt. What draws me to any character is complexity and understanding the balance. It’s almost anthropological in a way.

It was amazing. I was so terrified on day one. I’m always nervous about joining any show, doing any gig. But I remember day one of actually shooting with other cast members, turning around to Nick Müller, our A-camera operator, and I just went, “Look, Nick, you’ve been here way longer than I have. If I’m in your way, just tell me to fucking move.”

I’d been a part of Twilight as well—joined that on the second movie after watching a cultural moment explode—and I was in that position again with Stranger Things. It was so big. I was joining this new world, but everyone was wicked and super kind. I made some amazing friends. I love Millie [Bobby Brown]. She’s just the best. She’s like my little sister, and also like my big sister at times as well. She’s got so much sage advice and is so brilliant at what she does and so driven. I am in awe of her, and I was from the moment I met her.

I’ve got the hand of Vecna. I took it out on Fallon [the other] night. I told this story, but I got my bag searched in Mexico City on the way in over the weekend. We pulled up and one of the people there looked at me—her eyes got big. She said, “Vecna.” I’ve got three massive fuck-off suitcases. They’re going through them and I’m like, “Look, I’ve got the hand of Vecna in here. Do you want to see it?” And then it ended up being the quickest bag search ever. I got some elf ears with me as well, both made by the same guy, Barrie Gower.

It was the summer when I was 15. I spent it wearing a visor with spiky hair, because I used to skate growing up in super baggy jeans. I remember turning up being like, “That’s not you.” Skating is a part of who I am, but I was looking to represent myself in some way, shape, or form.

Then we started this indie band when I was 16, 17. Devonté Hynes had this band called Test Icicles. I always used to look at those guys with their skinny jeans and their big hair, and I was just like, “That’s a bit of me, that.” How skinny can my jeans get? How drain pipe-y am I? That’s where I really started to find my own identity.

I’ve been fortunate enough throughout my career to meet and work with such beautiful creative people in fashion and find myself more within that, too. I was talking about it to somebody yesterday: When you try a fit on that is not you, it’s like having a bad haircut. You don’t want to do that. I’m even the same if I’m doing a photoshoot. I always go through the rail and I’ll say, “That’s not my vibe. I can’t say that I’m going to wear that.” Of course, I’m always willing to try, I’m always willing to push. But you know yourself better as you get older.

It was from Alexander McQueen. I loved the identity of that brand, but I couldn’t afford a jacket, or a suit, or even a scarf. But the smaller pieces, the rings and the wallets, were like 100 bucks. Those were the things that I would gravitate towards and buy.

More recently, within the last 10 years, I remember coming here to New York for a show that I did called Will, going to Bergdorf, and buying a couple of pairs of Comme des Garçons trousers. As they were being rung up, I was like, “All right.” It wasn’t loads—we’re not talking thousands—but it was still a lot of money. That was probably the first big clothing purchase that I ever made. And I’ve still got the trousers. I used to wear them on stage in the band as well, which is foolish.

Got a bunch of stuff from H. Lorenzo the other day—some great shirts, some great jackets. I really like how they curate the store. My most recent purchase is a lot of stuff from the new Ann Demeulemeester collection. I actually just bought a sick leather trench from it—brown leather, which is fire.

Jacket by Thom Browne. Shirt, jeans, shoes by Ann Demeulemeester.

Going back to when we were kids: Test Icicles, the Libertines, the Rakes, Franz Ferdinand, Editors. Got to meet a few of those guys throughout my travels, which was always pretty sick. Nick Cave. Warren Ellis. Nick has got such a sharp style, as does Warren. Warren’s a bit more unbuttoned. I met Warren in Venice five years ago. He was stood at the end of the pier and I was so excited to meet him, I just bounded up. I was like, “Hi, Mr. Ellis. My name’s Jamie.” And I just blurted out to him for ages, and then I was like, “Thank you so much.” He said, "Good to meet you, mate. Bye.”

I think fluidity and being myself is always the main thing. I’ve never felt wholly comfortable in a regular suit. I remember we were invited to do a show in Venice, and the band that we were in was pretty heavy. We wore suits in an environment that for us felt almost quite subversive. The music that we played didn’t really fit that. I quite enjoyed that.

But on the whole, I don’t love suits too much. I like to keep it more interesting and fluid. I’m not saying that they can’t be interesting for other people, but I’ve never been interested [in them myself]. Apart from McQueen, but that’s because something like the McQueen shoulder is so identifiable and creates such an incredible silhouette. That’s probably the only time I’ve ever really been like, “I can wear this suit for a long time.” But yeah, I avoid anything that doesn’t feel right for me.

It’s hard to say. I do feel like so often they can blend. I’ve been so fortunate in my career, being drawn to things that feel like me and getting to explore different parts of myself on film. That does have an effect on the music that I’m making at the time.

With a film or a television series, you’re saying someone else’s words and building a character, but also at times injecting your own personal experience into that. In music, they are your words. You can make a choice to be like, “I’m going to build a world in this song to express something.” Or I can just be like, “This is me.” So, they can scratch different itches, but I think that they work in symbiosis sometimes.

The original movies came out when I was 12, so they were pretty seminal. I remember being in Hong Kong on a trip when The Hobbit was coming out. I was on my own, and I went to a cinema in a place called Pacific Place to watch it. That made a really big impact on me—it felt like a fantastical world that I could see myself in.

I started auditioning for it in 2024. Walking into it, of course, I was elated. I felt so lucky and so happy, like I was a little kid again. Like, I was 11 or 12 on stage in some provincial town outside of London, and now I get to fuckin’ walk into this Lord of the Rings world and be an elf? Dude, that’s sick.

Three non-negotiable albums that everyone… Oh, bloody Nora!

I discovered Dylan when I was like 16, when we were reading [J. D.] Salinger and Allen Ginsberg and books like On the Road. Let’s go with a classic. Freewheelin’ is old-school enough. It’s cool, pre-him going electric, which I adore as well. Highway 61 Revisited is a great record too. Take your pick between those two. Chopin’s Nocturnes are amazing. That’s a beautiful, beautiful piece to get into. Then there’s Nick Cave. I did an interview before and I chose Murder Ballads, which is a great record. But I also love some of the more recent work, like Ghosteen or Skeleton Tree. Ghosteen is amazing.

Oh, Ghosteen’s wicked. Let’s go with that. I referenced the artwork for Ghosteen on my last release. My album cover was by an artist called Thomas Cole, who did a collection of paintings about the journey from birth to death. He also did paintings of the Garden of Eden. From what I have now seen, those paintings heavily inspired the artist that did the paintings for Ghosteen as well, which is kind of insane.

So, he’s from the East. It’s the swearing.

#6684. Shop Our Favorite Celebrity Looks of the Week

Fall is finally here! If you’re wondering what to wear to embrace the drop in temperatures, we’re here to simplify matters with outfit ideas, courtesy of our favorite celebrities spotted on the streets. Consider this week’s edit your guide to everything from transitional fall looks to clever layering techniques, all infused with plenty of off-duty flair.

This week, celebrities embraced the seasonal chill, stepping out in their fall outerwear best. Jennifer Lawrence wore Auralee’s navy barn jacket for a walk in New York, styled with a graphic T-shirt, red pants, and a plaid button-down tied around her waist. Naomi Watts chose a double-breasted pinstripe blazer over a crisp white T-shirt and relaxed denim, finishing the look with playful accessories, including a floral brooch, an oversized-buckle belt, and a printed silk scarf. Both looks reinforced how a classic topper is truly the easiest way to pull together every fall outfit.

Meanwhile, guests at the CFDA Awards in New York offered a glimpse of what’s to come for occasion dressing as the holiday season approaches. Alexa Chung arrived in Tory Burch’s velvet robe dress and leather pumps in mustard tones, accessorizing with Elsa Peretti for Tiffany & Co. jewelry for a decadent finish. Hailey Bieber, too, embraced a gilded approach, leaning into the rich brocades and sumptuous embellishments seen on the spring 2027 runway. Her Saint Laurent skirt set, trimmed with faux-fur cuffs, was accented simply with strappy metallic heels for a touch of extra shine. Gold is having a moment, and there's no better time to embrace a little evening opulence for upcoming weddings, cocktail events, or festive celebrations.

Keep reading to discover these ideas and more, bringing timeless classics to life with a few standout finds, all reworked by the stars and completely shoppable.

Ahead, our favorite celeb outfits of the week.

Jennifer Lawrence was spotted wearing Auralee’s navy barn jacket for a walk in New York, styling it with her signature eclectic approach. Take cues from her layering technique, wearing it with a graphic Sesame Street T-shirt, baggy red pants, and a plaid button-down tied around the waist. Vans Authentic sneakers and oval rimless sunglasses rounded out the cool off-duty feel.

Alexa Chung arrived at the CFDA Awards in New York wearing Tory Burch’s mustard-toned velvet robe dress and leather pumps straight from the fall 2026 runway. Recreate the look with textural pieces in satin and velvet for a lesson in refined evening dressing. A black clutch bag and classic Elsa Peretti for Tiffany & Co. jewelry completed the look with a decadent touch.

Chloë Sevigny broke out her Fair Isle knitwear early, wearing a patterned sweater over a white polo shirt and denim midi skirt while out and about in New York. Tall leather boots with a Western-inspired spin, a slouchy hobo bag, and classic Wayfarer sunglasses gave the look a distinctly ‘70s-inspired aesthetic, with just the right amount of bohemian flair. Is it too early to start thinking about après-ski outfits? We think not.

Hailey Bieber brought a modern sensibility to old-world glamour at the CFDA Awards, leaning into the rich brocades and sumptuous embellishments seen at Anthony Vaccarello’s final spring 2027 show. She paired her Saint Laurent skirt set with strappy gold heels. We’d simply add a sleek clutch and delicate jewelry—a perfect festive look for any upcoming holiday cocktails or wedding celebrations.

While promoting the new season of All’s Fair, Naomi Watts stepped out in a double-breasted pinstripe blazer. The actress paired the jacket with a white T-shirt and relaxed denim, instead of the matching trousers, giving the tailored piece a more laid-back feel. When it came to accessories, however, she went all in, adding a floral brooch, an oversized-buckle belt, and a printed silk scarf. Here, more is more.

Rihanna made a case for easy monochrome dressing, wearing Phoebe Philo’s brown crewneck sweater with khaki trousers for a night out in Los Angeles. The trick is mixing complementary shades within the same color family. Minimalist pumps, oversized sunglasses, and understated jewelry—including diamond hoops and a metal choker necklace—take the look effortlessly from day to night.

Also on the press tour for All’s Fair, Sarah Paulson embraced maximalist dressing in a Michael Kors Collection look straight from the spring 2027 runway. Until it’s shoppable, recreate the idea with a striped rugby top, white button-down, and embellished satin skirt. Gray pumps lend an unexpected counterpoint, while diamond drop earrings and a ladylike top-handle bag round out the mix.

Want more? Shop the best celeb outfits from last week, below.

What’s more luxe than a sweeping velvet house coat? Jennifer Lawrence stepped out in New York in Colleen Allen’s stunning celery-green topper, making it the centerpiece of an otherwise understated look. The actress styled it simply with a white T-shirt and wide-leg trousers. Black velvet slippers and Tory Burch’s woven tote bag added tactile finishing touches, offering a lesson in maximalist proportions.

Gigi Hadid proved that a cozy cashmere set deserves to be seen. The supermodel layered Miu Miu’s waxed suede blazer over a gray V-neck cardigan and white T-shirt, swapping jeans for her Guest in Residence cashmere pants. Miu Miu’s cognac Pocket bag and suede loafers are her current accessory standbys, along with a zig-zag headband and oval glasses for playfulness—an easy off-duty look to recreate.

Katie Holmes wore a burgundy leather bomber jacket and striped sweater from Banana Republic’s recent collaboration with Zankov on a sunny day in New York. Although the knit has already sold out, a similar striped style offers the same eye-catching appeal. Paired with indigo barrel-leg jeans and soft leather loafers, Toteme’s T-lock bag and cat-eye sunglasses complete the city-ready feel.

For a chilly outing in London, Alexa Chung bundled up in Aligne’s gray faux-fur-trimmed wrap coat—the perfect topper to her signature T-shirt-and-jeans uniform. Black ballet heels and a Louis Vuitton shoulder bag reinforced the ladylike sensibility, while oversized sunnies brought a dose of downtown cool to the whole ensemble.

Hailey Bieber proves the easiest way to liven up wardrobe staples is with a bright outerwear piece. She added a cobalt pop to her black T-shirt and kick-flare trouser combination with a vibrant Mac coat, sticking to her go-to accessories: The Row’s Penelope mules and a burgundy flap shoulder bag. The result is an easy day-to-night formula for transitional weather.

Louisa Jacobson was spotted making the rounds on The Gilded Age press tour in a full look by Mel Usine. The ensemble comes straight from the brand’s spring 2027 collection and is available for pre-order. The actress made it her own with heeled peep-toe mules and sunglasses from Thistles (she’s a face of the brand). We’d simply add a standout mini bag to complete the look.

The groutfit is back. Meghann Fahy made a case for the simplicity of it all—wearing a matching Almina Concept shirt and trousers while promoting her new project, The Good Daughter. She kept things streamlined, accessorizing solely with glossy patent leather high-vamp pumps. Round out the look with a minimalist black bag, sleek sunglasses, and sculptural silver earrings.

Want more? Shop the best celeb outfits from last week, below.

Zoë Kravitz stepped out in New York three times this week wearing the same chocolate-brown windbreaker jacket. Here, the actress layered it over her signature go-tos: an all-black crewneck sweater with All Three’s flowy wide-leg pants. Burgundy ballet flats, red sunglasses, and an easy nylon tote bag completed the sporty-meets-minimalist aesthetic—in short, the perfect transitional fall look.

Although Jennifer Lawrence often gravitates towards elevated basics, she still likes to add a bit of quirk into the mix. For a walk in New York, she wore an oversized navy crewneck sweater with a black T-shirt, styling them with distressed straight-leg jeans in a light wash and brown suede mules. A bold lime-green handbag added a vibrant, unexpected pop to the otherwise understated outfit.

While in Rome, Julianne Moore went for Italian simplicity while promoting her new film, The Debut. Recreate her full Bottega Veneta look with a black ink-hued cardigan layered over a white long-sleeve T-shirt, adding the house’s statement skirt and black kitten-heeled mules for a fashion-forward finish. Accessorize with a clean clutch and silver jewelry for an effortless desk-to-dinner approach.

Dakota Johnson was spotted in Los Angeles continuing her new boho streak, this time in a vintage Simon & Garfunkel T-shirt and baggy brown corduroy pants. She kept it modern in the accessories department with Valentino’s patchwork Panthea bag, black ballet flats, and diamond drop earrings. Just add a leather jacket on chillier days for that extra rock-and-roll twist.

For a walk in London, Sienna Miller took a transitional approach to fall dressing, pairing a relaxed navy sweater with tailored black Bermuda shorts. Knee-high leather boots and Bottega Veneta’s Cabat bag lent a dose of designer flair, while black aviator-inspired frames added a cool, off-duty edge. This one works just as well for weekend wanderings as it does for a casual office setting.

For an outing in New York, Karlie Kloss wore a cream pintucked blouse with a gray mini skirt, draping a cozy cashmere shawl over the shoulders to ward off unexpected chills. Black ballet flats, a structured everyday bag, and oval sunnies pulled the look together with signature flair. Consider this an easy office look to keep in rotation, especially on those in-between-season days.

Want more? Shop the best celeb outfits from last week, below.

For a day of shopping in Paris, Zendaya relied on a familiar combination: a simple white T-shirt and blue denim, with a few unexpected twists. The actress topped her cuffed jeans off with a black leather coat (hers was vintage Prada), accessorizing with Maison Margiela Tabi wedges and tiny sunglasses for a dose of downtown ’90s cool with a distinctly modern edge.

While filming her new project Die Alive in New York, Zoë Kravitz was spotted in a chocolate-brown mac coat layered over a gray camisole and a vintage Miu Miu slip skirt in lime green. Paired with Jude’s high-vamp pumps and an archival Fendi Baguette bag (we found the modern take), the look makes a compelling case for elevating rich autumnal tones with an unexpected pop of color.

Julianne Moore rarely strays from her signature uniform of minimalist wardrobe staples, and her head-to-toe Bottega Veneta look is proof. Re-create it with a boxy navy knit top and black pleated trousers, then add the house’s signature touches: white glove pumps, a roomy Intrecciato shoulder bag, and black oval sunglasses. Red earrings offer a playful finishing touch.

Monica Barbaro embraced the classic fall uniform in London, choosing Me+Em’s houndstooth Pub jacket as her statement layer. Worn with a white crewneck T-shirt, wide-leg jeans, and pointy black boots, the look is quintessential fall dressing at its best—an undeniable combination for work, weekend, and beyond. Simply grab a suede tote and minimal jewelry to round out the easy, everyday feel.

Keri Russell brought her signature polish to New York, styling a black crewneck sweater with tweed Bermuda shorts—a clever way for keeping them in rotation a little longer. Louis Vuitton’s Speedy Bandoulière bag rounded out her classic look, with Saint Laurent’s pointed-toe pumps and Ray-Ban Wayfarers as her elegant finishing touches.

Daisy Edgar-Jones traded Sense and Sensibility cosplay for something more subtle, while continuing the press tour in New York. Taking one of fall’s biggest denim trends for a test drive, the actress paired a white T-shirt and classic straight-leg jeans with Burberry’s cropped trench jacket and Bridle saddle bag. Pointy pumps and sleek sunglasses gave the look a little urban flair.

Kendall Jenner stepped out for dinner in Los Angeles in an understated look worth bookmarking. A black bateau-neck top and navy slip skirt (yes, the two shades work together!) took on an elevated feel alongside The Row’s flat mules and camel Terrasse shoulder bag. Add the supermodel’s signature silver hoop earrings and favorite Chimi sunglasses as effortless accents.

Elizabeth Debicki is redefining the modern suit. The Wicker actress wore a gray tailored look from Aflalo while promoting her new film in New York, demonstrating how the right silhouette can keep suiting feeling fresh. A nipped-waist blazer and tapered trousers strike the right balance between sharp and streamlined; just add pumps and a hardworking shoulder bag for days at the office.

Want more? Shop the best celeb outfits from last week, below.

It’s finally jacket weather in New York, and Zoë Kravitz made a case for suede outerwear, building her fall look around a sumptuous knee-length coat. True to form, the actress kept the rest of her outfit pared back, but surprised in the accessories department. Patent knee-high boots brought edge, while her now-signature purple scarf added a vibrant pop—proving that even minimalists can appreciate a jolt of color.

Gigi Hadid touched down in Paris for Fashion Week, bringing her clean-girl aesthetic to the city’s cobblestoned streets. Relying on Americana staples to anchor the look—a crisp white button-down shirt paired with blue bootcut jeans—she gave the classic combination a playful twist with floral-embroidered mesh flats, her favorite brown shoulder bag, and a zigzag tortoise headband—essentially the perfect off-duty outfit.

Paloma Elsesser stepped out in the City of Light for the Loewe show, donning a cropped shearling jacket—yes, it’s about that time to take yours out. The supermodel paired the camel confection with a navy pencil skirt for a polished take on fall dressing, bringing in even more texture and color with emerald green pumps and the house’s Whisker bag in a bold checked pattern.

Forget the funnel-neck jacket—Sarah Pidgeon proved this season is all about cinched-waist styles in leather. The actress attended the Balenciaga show wearing a dressed-up take on the trend, offset by split-hem blue jeans for cool contrast. Black pointy pumps and her small Rodeo handbag brought a little downtown attitude to this Parisian street style moment.

Alexa Chung’s signature preppy polish was in full effect at the Miu Miu show in Paris, where she styled a chunky striped cardigan over a delicate camisole. The cozy layers softened this otherwise hyper-feminine look, which included a pencil skirt, pointed pumps, and a top-handle bag.

For dinner at Caviar Kaspia, Emma Stone went for sophisticated, not fussy, pairing a structured jacket with relaxed straight-leg jeans from Still Here. Strappy black sandals (hers are past-season Khaite) elevated the transitional look, proving that elegant evening attire doesn’t have to mean overdoing it. Add a sleek belt and a stylish crossbody, and you’re ready for a night out.

Back in New York, Jennifer Lawrence experimented with silhouette and texture, pairing Dissh’s Ryker blazer with Pauline Dujancourt’s draped chiffon skirt in a lilac hue. Both are now sold out, but you can recreate the idea with similar styles, playing with the contrast between structure and fluidity. The actress kept it strictly designer in the accessories department, with Phoebe Philo’s small Gig bag and Dior Oblique sunglasses, while satin mules and turquoise necklaces brought in unexpected twists.

Hailey Bieber is also on board with making jeans a little more glamorous by using a little black jacket. Her embellished leather topper came straight off the Magda Butrym spring 2027 runway—you’ll have to wait a little to get your hands on it—but the overall idea is one to steal now. Minimalist mule sandals, a sleek clutch, and diamond drop earrings keep things firmly in evening territory, while her ball cap offers an easy day-to-night switch-up.
